Fix your damn game.

The audio quality is being obliterated on startup. I tried manually setting the microphone. removing the headset. changing the headset. turning off the mic. Setting communications device manually. But the game refused to use anything besides my headset mic no matter what. So it would wreck my audio fidelity. 

Its completely asinine to not let the player choose an audio output. No other game does this. I legit contacted xbox support and they told me to buy a new headset. I will change my review when they add the ability to change your audio output.

Amazing pirate vibe, but highly frustrating for solo players.
​I really want to love this game because the sailing and world-building are top-notch. However, as a solo player, the experience is underwhelming compared to games like AC Black Flag where you have full control over your ship.
​In Sea of Thieves, if you want to sail a bigger ship, you are forced to play multiplayer with real people. Matchmaking with strangers isn't always reliable, and not everyone has a group of friends available to play. Why not allow solo players to fully control larger ships, even if it requires a heavy grind to unlock that privilege?
​It feels like the game punishes you just for playing alone. Great game overall, but needs better balance for solo captains.

A good pirate experience, beautiful sailing mechanics and water, low hardware requirements, fun dungeons and treasuring grabbing experiences. Main downside is that it's a "friends" game, you can technically play it solo, but it wont be that fun compared to a group play session. Overall a pretty good game to buy when it's half off or more ($20 or less), really wish it was smaller though, 130gb for this is crazy.

citations.review_text:
Sea of Thieves is a game I wanted to love more than I actually did.

The idea is incredible. Sailing around with a crew, hunting treasure, customizing your pirate, fighting skeletons, exploring islands, getting into dumb ocean chaos, and living out the whole pirate fantasy should have been exactly my kind of thing.

And there are definitely moments where it works. The water is gorgeous, the sailing feels good, the world has charm, and when you are with the right people, the game can be genuinely fun. There is something great about being on a ship with friends, yelling about repairs, crashing into things, playing music, and pretending any of you know what you are doing.

But I always wanted more from it.

More customization. More player-friendly systems. More ways to enjoy the world without constantly feeling like PvP was lurking over your shoulder with a cannonball and a bad attitude.

It took years for them to add a more solo-friendly experience without PvP, and even then, the rewards and treasure are reduced compared to the full PvP mode. I get that the main game is built around shared-world risk, but it still feels rough when people just want to enjoy the pirate adventure without being punished for not wanting to deal with other players.

Sea of Thieves has so much potential, and sometimes it really does feel magical. But it also feels like a game that made me keep saying, “This could be amazing if it just gave me a little more room to enjoy it my way.”

I wanted the pirate dream.

Instead, I got a beautiful ocean, a good concept, and a lot of frustration floating beside the ship.

Game still treats its PVE players like second class citizens, spitting on them at every chance they get, locking reputation to a measly 25, cutting gold earnings locking content that would be fun to do in PVE>

Ugliest character creator in all of gaming history, every single girl looks like a man with a jawline that could cut GLASS They claimed originally it was to stop everyone from making jack sparrow, then go a head and add his cosmetics! 
you will want to buy a mask just to cover the pirates face. 

All in all, if i had not got this game on super duper mega sale i would not have bothered to keep it.

Sea of Thieves taught me two very important life lessons: never trust other pirates… and trust your friends even less.

It all started with “hey, let’s have a chill sailing session.” Five minutes later our ship was on fire, one friend was playing the accordion instead of helping, another was trying to sell treasure we didn’t even have yet, and I got eaten by a shark for the third time.

This game is absolutely amazing if you enjoy chaos, betrayal, and moments where someone yells “I GOT THE LOOT!” just to fall into the ocean immediately after. Every session is a new story — sometimes an epic adventure, sometimes two hours of grinding treasure just to get sunk by another crew in 15 seconds.

The graphics are beautiful, the sea looks so good you almost want to drown in it (and you will, a lot). The mechanics are simple but super fun, especially when you’re trying to manage the ship while someone is actively shooting you with a cannon.

Do I recommend it? Yes.

Will you suffer? Also yes.

10/10 would get robbed by other pirates again.

DO NOT, AND I MEAN DO NOT PURCHASE THIS GAME IN 2026

I played this game back in the beta days and at launch. I probably soaked up at least 500+ hours into it when it was new. Took a long hiatus from it when the sweats and exploiters started to show up. Recently got back on after seeing that the game was all but dead at this point and i can tell you first hand that it is far worse than it was in the beginning.
The PVE activities are a blast, but the community of players that still populate this game are by far the most annoying and aggressive player base I've had the displeasure of running across.

If you're new to the game, DO NOT expect any help from other players. 
Open crew? - Odds are you'll be joined by someone who will sink your ship and leave. 
Find another ship? - They'll sink you on sight. 
Want to play casually and grind peacefully? - You will be hunted down and griefed.

The game offers a PVE mode that limits your ability to progress and fully explore the Emissaries and basically tries strong arming you into joining the parasitic cesspool of High Seas.

The game wants you to spend hours on end grinding your heart out just for all of it to be taken away in 30 seconds by a team who plays the game like a 9-5 job and only exist to cause you torment.

The game is thankfully dying fast and hopefully Rare does the right thing and takes restrictions off the PVE game mode and allows the casual audience to finally be able to enjoy the game. It may not save them, but it would at least stop the bleeding.

*Edit* Dude who commented is either a paid moderator or something wrong in the head. Check the community threads and you'll see he's commented on damn near every post and definitely every post criticizing this game and its malignant player base* - And yes the game is dying. Check current peak player count.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the player-versus-player encounters and open-world combat can be brutal and punishing for newcomers trying to learn the game.

citations.review_text:
This game is basically friendship, violence, and bad decisions on a boat. 

The sailing is genuinely satisfying, the atmosphere is beautiful, and the amount of random ♥♥♥♥ that can happen is insane. One minute you're peacefully delivering cargo, next minute some sweaty pirate crew is chasing you across the entire map while your ship is on fire and your friend is screaming about the holes in the hull.

And honestly, that's the charm.

The game isn't really about grinding for some insane meta build. It's about the stories you accidentally create with your crew. Getting betrayed, accidentally sinking yourself, stealing someone's treasure, getting jumped by a Kraken, or spending 20 minutes trying to park the ship properly.

That said, the PvP can be brutal, especially when you're still learning, and some sessions can feel like you spent more time sailing than actually accomplishing anything. But when everything clicks? Absolutely peak.

Would recommend if you have friends to play with.

Solo is doable, but with a crew, this game becomes a completely different experience.

After spending a lot of time in Sea of Thieves, I can confidently say it's one of the most memorable multiplayer games I've played. Every voyage feels different. You might set out to dig up treasure, only to end up in a naval battle, fighting a Kraken, or making an unexpected alliance with another crew.

The sailing mechanics are fantastic and reward teamwork. Whether you're adjusting sails, patching holes, or firing cannons, everyone has a role to play. The world is also gorgeous, with stunning oceans, dynamic weather, and islands that are genuinely fun to explore.

One thing to keep in mind is that the game can be unforgiving. You can lose hours of treasure to another crew if you're not careful, but that's also what makes every successful haul so satisfying. The progression is mostly cosmetic, so the focus stays on improving your skills rather than grinding for better gear.

This game is at its best with friends, but even solo players can have incredible adventures if they're willing to learn. If you enjoy open-world sandbox games where every session creates its own story, Sea of Thieves is absolutely worth playing.

Recommended.

Sea of Thieves delivers one of the most unique pirate experiences available today. From sailing across vast oceans to hunting treasure, battling skeletons, and engaging in intense naval combat, the game creates moments that few other multiplayer titles can match. The art style is beautiful, the world feels alive, and the ocean physics remain some of the best in gaming.

Playing with friends is where Sea of Thieves truly shines. Coordinating a crew, taking on world events, and fighting rival pirates can lead to unforgettable adventures and plenty of laughs. The freedom to create your own stories is one of the game's greatest strengths.

Unfortunately, the experience is held back by several issues. The gameplay loop can become repetitive over time, with many activities feeling similar after dozens of hours. Solo players may struggle against larger crews, and progression is mostly limited to cosmetic rewards. The game also suffers from occasional bugs and technical issues, ranging from minor annoyances to glitches that can disrupt gameplay and take away from the overall experience.

While the PvP system adds excitement and tension, losing hard-earned loot to another crew can sometimes feel more frustrating than rewarding. Despite years of updates and new content, Sea of Thieves still relies heavily on players creating their own fun rather than providing a strong sense of progression.

Overall, Sea of Thieves is a fun and visually impressive pirate sandbox that offers some incredible multiplayer moments. However, repetitive gameplay, limited progression, and occasional bugs prevent it from fully living up to its potential.

Final Rating: 6.5/10

I really enjoy this game and think it offers an overall great experience. The graphics are impressive, the gameplay is engaging, and the sense of adventure keeps me coming back.

That said, I wish the game had fewer bugs and better matchmaking. One of the biggest issues is highly experienced players constantly attacking newer or lower-level players, which can make it difficult for new players to enjoy the game. Instead of pushing new players to Safe Seas, I think the game would benefit from a skill-based matchmaking system that pairs crews of similar experience. This would create a more balanced and enjoyable experience for everyone while still preserving the excitement of PvP.

claims.claim: Reviewers report an increasing push toward microtransactions and a paid battle pass, with quality cosmetics placed behind the Pirate Emporium store or a PvP grind.

citations.review_text:
I fu-cking love Sea of Thieves. But this adoration comes with a huge caveat: Only when I play it with my friends. 

Playing this game with a full galleon of my favourite people in a Discord call together is some of the most fun I've EVER had in a videogame and I think those moments are genuinely unmatched. So much so that I have 100 hours in this game and maybe 5 of them were just me on my own. So much so that I made TWO hours of YouTube videos of just me and my friends messing around in the game and accomplishing nothing specific. We played so much of this game we have developed specific terminology to describe things in game and our own methodology to completing tasks and farming resources. 

I genuinely adore this game so much and yet at 112GBs of size I just cannot justify reinstalling this game when I can't guarantee that I'll be able to get everyone on board (haha get it?) in a world where Sea of Thieves literally has a paid battlepass and seasonal challenges in a game that costs 40 f-ucking Great British Pounds. 

I love so much about this game, if you are in a group of good friends just looking to mess around and maybe sink a few noobs but at the same time, the rampant and blatant cheaters, absolutely no-life sweats that take you down in 4 seconds flat, and again, incredibly predatory monetisation is very off-putting.

I fu-cking love Sea of Thieves. But this adoration comes with a huge caveat: Only when I play it with my friends. 

Playing this game with a full galleon of my favourite people in a Discord call together is some of the most fun I've EVER had in a videogame and I think those moments are genuinely unmatched. So much so that I have 100 hours in this game and maybe 5 of them were just me on my own. So much so that I made TWO hours of YouTube videos of just me and my friends messing around in the game and accomplishing nothing specific. We played so much of this game we have developed specific terminology to describe things in game and our own methodology to completing tasks and farming resources.
